explanation.en:
How it works:
A conditional sentence with "if" sets up a condition and its result. The First Conditional (if + present, will + base verb) covers real or likely situations. The Second Conditional (if + past, would + base verb) handles hypothetical or unlikely ones. In song lyrics, conditionals create emotional stakes — "what if this happens?"

Example from this song:
"If I lose it all" — a real conditional presenting a plausible, terrifying scenario. The singer contemplates the possibility of losing everything and what emotional state would follow.

More examples:
• "If the walls fall, we fall with them" — real condition tied to a consequence
• "If I had wings, I would fly away" — hypothetical (Second Conditional)
• "If you leave, nothing remains" — condition with devastating result

grammar_points.name: Present Continuous for dramatic effect (-ing forms)

explanation.en:
How it works:
The Present Continuous tense (am/is/are + verb-ing) normally describes actions happening right now. In song lyrics, -ing forms are used without the auxiliary verb ("burning" instead of "I am burning") to create immediacy, urgency, and visceral tension. This stripped-down style makes the listener feel they are inside the moment.

Example from this song:
"I'm tearless, I'm fearless, I'm burning" — the -ing form "burning" creates a sense of ongoing, present intensity. "Coming for you" — the progressive creates approaching danger.

More examples:
• "Still wandering in the deep mist" — ongoing, atmospheric image
• "The world is crumbling" — present continuous for dramatic tension
• "Hearts are breaking, walls are shaking" — parallel -ing forms for rhythm and urgency

grammar_points.name: "All I ever wanted" — emphatic past desire

explanation.en:
How it works:
The pattern "All I ever wanted to do was..." is an emphatic structure that distills someone's deepest, most genuine desire into a single statement. "All" means "the only thing," "ever" spans their entire life, and "wanted" places it in the past. Together, it creates a powerful gap between pure intention and tragic outcome — "I only wanted one simple thing, and yet..."

Example from this song:
"All I ever wanted to do was do right things. I never wanted to be the king." — The singer (from Eren's perspective) emphasizes that their original desire was simple and noble, but fate twisted it into something monstrous.

More examples:
• "All I ever wanted was to be free" — simple desire, complex reality
• "All she ever wanted was to be loved" — poignant gap between wish and outcome
• "All we ever wanted was peace" — collective desire contrasted with war

grammar_points.name: German song - no Japanese grammar

explanation.en:
This song is entirely in German. The vocabulary section provides Japanese equivalents of key German words for educational cross-referencing. Attack on Titan frequently uses German in its soundtrack to evoke the European medieval atmosphere of the walled cities.

While no Japanese grammar structures appear in the lyrics, the vocabulary maps German concepts like Mauer (壁, kabe, "wall"), Schicksal (運命, unmei, "fate"), and Flugel (翼, tsubasa, "wings") to their Japanese counterparts.

grammar_points.conjugation_path: N/A

grammar_points.name: 〜まで (made - until)

explanation.en:
The Japanese equivalent of German "bis" (until) as used in this song. まで (made) marks a temporal or spatial endpoint, meaning "until" or "up to."

How it works:
Place まで (made) after a noun (time/place) or a verb in dictionary form. It sets the boundary or limit.

Example from this song:
"Wir werden kampfen bis dieser heisse Wind unsere Flugel nimmt" → 風が翼を奪うまで戦う (kaze ga tsubasa o ubau made tatakau, "fight until the wind takes our wings")

More examples:
- 5時まで待つ (goji made matsu, "wait until 5 o'clock")
- 東京まで行く (toukyou made iku, "go up to Tokyo")
- 終わるまで頑張る (owaru made ganbaru, "keep trying until it's over")

grammar_points.conjugation_path: 戦う (tatakau) + まで (made) → 風が翼を奪うまで戦う (kaze ga tsubasa o ubau made tatakau, "fight until the wind takes our wings")

grammar_points.name: 〜ことができる (koto ga dekiru - can do)

explanation.en:
The Japanese equivalent of German "kann" (can) as used in this song. This pattern expresses ability or possibility.

How it works:
Take the dictionary form of a verb, add こと (koto) + が (ga) + できる (dekiru). Together: "can do [verb]."

Example from this song:
"Sogar ein kleiner Vogel kann frei uber die Mauer fliegen" → 飛ぶことができる (tobu koto ga dekiru, "can fly")

More examples:
- 読むことができる (yomu koto ga dekiru, "can read")
- ピアノを弾くことができます (piano o hiku koto ga dekimasu, "I can play the piano")
- 一人で料理することができた (hitori de ryouri suru koto ga dekita, "I was able to cook by myself")

grammar_points.conjugation_path: 飛ぶ (tobu) → 飛ぶことができる (tobu koto ga dekiru, "can fly")

grammar_points.name: Literary negative attributives 〜なき / 〜ぬ

explanation.en:
Classical Japanese had two negative endings — 〜ぬ and 〜ず — that survive in modern usage as literary alternatives to 〜ない. When attached attributively (modifying a noun), 〜ぬ feels stately, and 〜なき (a related classical adjective ending) is used for the negation of i-adjectives or for fixed compound expressions.

This song uses both: 限りなき ('boundless' — 限りない in literary form) in 限りなきチカラ, and 変わらぬ ('unchanging' — 変わらない in literary form) in 変わらぬキズナ. Both modify nouns directly with elevated, almost epic register.

For most verbs the form is verb (negative stem) + ぬ: 知らぬ ('not knowing'), 見ぬ ('not seen'), 行かぬ ('not going'). 〜なき attaches to い-stems: 限りない → 限りなき, さえなき, 数なき. Other typical examples: 限りなき愛 ('boundless love'), 変わらぬ友情 ('unchanging friendship'), 動かぬ証拠 ('immovable evidence'), 知らぬ顔 ('a face that doesn't know — feigned ignorance').

grammar_points.conjugation_path: verb (negative stem) + ぬ; i-adj 〜ない → 〜なき (literary attributive)

grammar_points.name: 〜ならば (literary conditional 'if (it is the case)')

explanation.en:
ならば is the literary form of なら, both meaning 'if (X) is the case'. Like なら, it takes an established premise and asks 'if (that) is so, then...'. The longer ならば feels more elevated, fitting song lyrics, formal speech, and old-fashioned dialogue.

This song uses ならば twice in parallel: 求めるならば ('if you seek') and 躊躇うならば ('if you hesitate'), each setting up the verse's conditional reach. Verse 19 uses the shorter なら (進みゆく航路なら).

Other typical examples: 行くならば早く ('if you're going, go quickly'), 信じるならば疑うな ('if you believe, don't doubt'), あなたならば理解できる ('if it's you, you'll understand'), 雨ならば中止 ('cancelled if it rains').

grammar_points.conjugation_path: plain-form predicate + (の)ならば; na-adj/noun + (なら)ば; literary register

grammar_points.name: 〜ために (for the sake of; in order to)

explanation.en:
ために (literally 'for the sake of') attached to a plain-form verb expresses purpose: 'in order to (do X)'. Attached to a noun + の it means 'for the sake of (X)'. Distinct from causal use 〜ため(に) ('because of').

This song uses ために twice in close parallel: 信じるもの守るために ('to protect what you believe in') and 自分らしく笑うために ('to laugh as your true self'). Each frames the song's emotional 'Cry' as purposeful.

Other typical examples: 健康のために運動する ('I exercise for my health'), 君のために頑張る ('I'll do my best for you'), 試験に合格するために勉強する ('I study (in order) to pass the exam'), 平和のために戦う ('to fight for peace').

grammar_points.conjugation_path: verb (plain form) + ために; noun + のために (purpose; not causal)

grammar_points.name: 〜らしく (in the manner of; befitting)

explanation.en:
〜らしい attached to a noun makes a quality-adjective meaning '(in a way) befitting / typical of (X)'. The adverbial form 〜らしく describes an action done in that manner.

This song uses 自分らしく ('in a way befitting yourself / true to yourself') in 自分らしく笑うために. The phrase carries the moral weight of 'authentically' — laughing as you really are, not as others expect.

Distinguish from 〜らしい meaning 'I hear that...' (hearsay). Other typical examples: 男らしく振る舞う ('to act like a man'), 子供らしく遊ぶ ('to play in a childlike way'), あなたらしくない ('that's not like you'), 春らしい一日 ('a springlike day').

grammar_points.conjugation_path: noun + らしい (quality-adj) → adverbial 〜らしく

grammar_points.name: Volitional 〜よう / 〜う (let's...; intent)

explanation.en:
The volitional form expresses 'let's (do)' or the speaker's intent. For Group 1 verbs the final -u shifts to -ō (祈る → 祈ろう, 振りかざす → 振りかざそう). Group 2: -る → -よう (信じている → 信じていよう, 探し出す happens to be Group 1 → 探し出そう). Irregulars: する → しよう, 来る → 来よう.

This song chains volitionals across the chorus: 振りかざそう, 祈ろう, 探し出そう, 信じていよう. Each rallies the listener to share the speaker's resolve — an unbroken chain of 'let's'.

Other typical examples: 一緒に行こう ('let's go together'), 早く帰ろう ('let's head home soon'), 頑張ろう ('let's give it our best'), 信じよう ('let's believe').

grammar_points.conjugation_path: Group 1: -u → -ō; Group 2: -る → -よう; irregular: する → しよう, 来る → 来よう

grammar_points.name: 〜べき (should; ought to)

explanation.en:
〜べき attached to a plain-form verb expresses 'should (do X)' or 'ought to'. It carries moral or logical obligation — stronger than 〜方がいい. The form is classical-derived and slightly formal. する becomes すべき (or するべき).

This song uses 還るべき場所 ('the place I should return to') in 君と還るべき場所がある. The 〜べき turns 還る into a moral imperative: not just 'a place to go back to', but 'a place I'm meant to return to'.

Other typical examples: やるべきこと ('things one should do'), 知るべき真実 ('a truth one should know'), 守るべき約束 ('a promise one should keep'), 言うべきだ ('one should say it'). Negative: 〜べきではない ('shouldn't').

grammar_points.conjugation_path: verb (plain form) + べき; する → すべき (literary) or するべき

grammar_points.name: 〜ても (temo - even if)

explanation.en:
Expresses "even if" — the result does not change regardless of the condition.

How it works:
Take the て-form (te-form) of a verb and add も (mo).

Example from this song:
追いかけても遅く遠く (oikakete mo osoku tooku, "Even if I chase after you, it's too late, too far")

More examples:
- 走っても間に合わない (hashitte mo ma ni awanai, "Even if I run, I won't make it")
- 頑張っても無理だった (ganbatte mo muri datta, "Even if I tried hard, it was impossible")
- お金があっても幸せじゃない (okane ga atte mo shiawase ja nai, "Even with money, you're not happy")

grammar_points.conjugation_path: 追いかける (oikakeru) → 追いかけて (oikakete, te-form) → 追いかけても (oikakete mo, "even if I chase")

grammar_points.name: 〜ことも＋なく (koto mo naku - without even)

explanation.en:
Expresses that something does not happen, with emphasis on "not even." It combines こと (koto, "the act of") + も (mo, "even") + なく (naku, "without").

How it works:
Verb dictionary form + ことも + なく. It means "without even [doing X]."

Example from this song:
時が止まることもなく (toki ga tomaru koto mo naku, "Without time ever stopping")

More examples:
- 振り返ることもなく去った (furikaeru koto mo naku satta, "Left without even looking back")
- 休むこともなく働いた (yasumu koto mo naku hataraita, "Worked without even resting")
- 迷うこともなく答えた (mayou koto mo naku kotaeta, "Answered without even hesitating")

Many anime songs mix English and Japanese in the same song. This is called code-switching. English lines often carry universally accessible emotional statements, while Japanese lines add poetic depth and cultural nuance.

How it works:
The songwriter freely alternates between languages, using English for chorus hooks ("Don't you wanna stay with me?") and Japanese for emotional depth (追いかけても遅く遠く, oikakete mo osoku tooku).

Example from this song:
"I'll be waiting for you" alternates with 問いかけに答えはなく (toikake ni kotae wa naku, "There is no answer to my questioning")

This technique is common in SiM, ONE OK ROCK, and many anime soundtrack artists.

grammar_points.name: 〜ぐらいなら (gurai nara - rather than)

explanation.en:
Expresses a strong preference: "rather than doing X (which is undesirable), I would choose Y instead." The speaker considers X so bad that anything else is better.

How it works:
Attach ぐらいなら (gurai nara) after the dictionary form of a verb. The clause that follows states the preferred alternative.

Example from this song:
傷ついた足を休ませるぐらいなら (kizutsuita ashi o yasumaseru gurai nara, "Rather than resting your wounded legs...")

More examples:
- 嘘をつくぐらいなら黙ったほうがいい (uso o tsuku gurai nara damatta hou ga ii, "Rather than lie, it's better to stay silent")
- 諦めるぐらいなら最後まで戦う (akirameru gurai nara saigo made tatakau, "Rather than give up, I'll fight to the end")
- 待つぐらいなら自分で行く (matsu gurai nara jibun de iku, "Rather than wait, I'll go myself")

grammar_points.conjugation_path: 休ませる (yasumaseru) + ぐらいなら (gurai nara) → 休ませるぐらいなら (yasumaseru gurai nara, "rather than resting")

grammar_points.name: 〜続ける (tsuzukeru - continue doing)

explanation.en:
An auxiliary verb meaning "to keep doing" or "to continue doing." Attach it to the stem of another verb to express an ongoing, uninterrupted action.

How it works:
Take the masu-stem of a verb (remove ます), then add 続ける (tsuzukeru).

Example from this song:
信じ続けるだけが答えじゃない (shinji tsuzukeru dake ga kotae ja nai, "Just keeping on believing isn't the answer")

More examples:
- 走り続ける (hashiri tsuzukeru, "to keep running")
- 歌い続けた (utai tsuzuketa, "kept singing")
- 彼は努力し続けている (kare wa doryoku shi tsuzukete iru, "He keeps on making effort")

grammar_points.conjugation_path: 信じる (shinjiru) → 信じ (shinji, masu-stem) + 続ける (tsuzukeru) → 信じ続ける (shinji tsuzukeru, "keep believing")

grammar_points.name: 〜なければならない (nakereba naranai - must do)

explanation.en:
Expresses obligation: "must do" or "have to do." In this song, it is used in its negative implication: "if you don't do X, Y won't happen."

How it works:
Take the negative form of a verb (ない), replace ない with なければ (nakereba), then add ならない (naranai). It literally means "if [not doing X], it won't do."

Example from this song:
もがき続けなければ始まらない (mogaki tsuzukenakereba hajimaranai, "If you don't keep struggling, nothing begins")

More examples:
- 勉強しなければならない (benkyou shinakereba naranai, "I must study")
- 早く起きなければならない (hayaku okinakereba naranai, "I have to wake up early")
- 薬を飲まなければならない (kusuri o nomanakereba naranai, "I must take medicine")

grammar_points.conjugation_path: もがく (mogaku) → もがき続ける (mogaki tsuzukeru) → もがき続けなければ (mogaki tsuzukenakereba, "if you don't keep struggling")

grammar_points.name: 〜としても (toshitemo - even if)

explanation.en:
A concessive conditional meaning "even if" or "even assuming that." The speaker acknowledges a difficult hypothetical but declares their intention regardless.

How it works:
Attach としても (toshitemo) after the plain form of a verb or adjective + だ (da). The main clause states what the speaker will do despite the condition.

Example from this song:
翳したプライドが間違いだとしても (kazashita puraido ga machigai da toshitemo, "Even if the pride I held up was a mistake")

More examples:
- 失敗したとしても後悔しない (shippai shita toshitemo koukai shinai, "Even if I fail, I won't regret it")
- 雨が降るとしても行く (ame ga furu toshitemo iku, "Even if it rains, I'll go")
- 高いとしても買いたい (takai toshitemo kaitai, "Even if it's expensive, I want to buy it")

grammar_points.conjugation_path: 間違いだ (machigai da) + としても (toshitemo) → 間違いだとしても (machigai da toshitemo, "even if it's a mistake")

grammar_points.name: 命令形 (meireikei - imperative form)

explanation.en:
The direct command form of verbs. It is a forceful way to tell someone to do something, commonly used in rallying cries, sports, and passionate lyrics like this song.

How it works:
For godan (u-) verbs: change the final う (u) sound to え (e).
For ichidan (ru-) verbs: replace る (ru) with ろ (ro).

Example from this song:
進め (susume, "Advance!") and 突き破れ (tsukiyabure, "Break through!")

More examples:
- 行け (ike, "Go!")
- 食べろ (tabero, "Eat!")
- 立て (tate, "Stand up!")

grammar_points.conjugation_path: 進む (susumu) → 進め (susume, "advance!"), 突き破る (tsukiyaburu) → 突き破れ (tsukiyabure, "break through!")

grammar_points.name: 〜かける (kakeru - about to; on the verge of)

explanation.en:
Attached to a verb stem, かける (kakeru) indicates an action that has started but is not yet complete, or something on the verge of happening. Think of it as "half-done" or "about to."

How it works:
Take the masu-stem of a verb and add かける (kakeru).

Example from this song:
描いてた理想が崩れかけても (egaiteta risou ga kuzure kakete mo, "Even if the ideal I envisioned is about to crumble")

More examples:
- 死にかけた (shinikaketa, "almost died")
- 言いかけてやめた (iikakete yameta, "started to say something but stopped")
- 食べかけのりんご (tabekake no ringo, "a half-eaten apple")

grammar_points.conjugation_path: 崩れる (kuzureru) → 崩れ (kuzure, masu-stem) + かける (kakeru) → 崩れかける (kuzurekakeru, "about to crumble")

explanation.en:
This song is entirely in German. It is one of the most iconic emotional pieces in Attack on Titan, reflecting themes of mortality, beauty, and fighting against fate.

The vocabulary section is empty for this track because the German lyrics do not map directly to beginner Japanese grammar. However, key concepts from this song have Japanese equivalents:
- Leben (life) = 命 (inochi) or 人生 (jinsei)
- Schicksal (fate) = 運命 (unmei)
- Licht (light) = 光 (hikari)
- Kinder (children) = 子供たち (kodomo-tachi)

The Japanese equivalent of German "gegen" (against) as used in this song. It expresses direction of action toward a target.

How it works:
Place に対して (ni taishite) after a noun to indicate "against" or "toward" that thing.

Example from this song:
"Wir werden gegen unser Schicksal ankaempfen" → 運命に対して戦う (unmei ni taishite tatakau, "fight against fate")

More examples:
- 敋に対して戦う (teki ni taishite tatakau, "fight against the enemy")
- 問題に対して行動する (mondai ni taishite koudou suru, "take action against the problem")
- 自分に対して正直である (jibun ni taishite shoujiki de aru, "be honest with yourself")

The Japanese equivalent of German "irgendwann" (someday) from this song. It expresses an indefinite future time.

How it works:
いつか (itsuka) is an adverb placed before the verb. It means "someday" or "one day."

Example from this song:
"Hoffentlich koennen wir es irgendwann verstehen" → いつか理解できるといい (itsuka rikai dekiru to ii, "I hope we can understand someday")

More examples:
- いつか日本に行きたい (itsuka nihon ni ikitai, "I want to go to Japan someday")
- いつか分かるだろう (itsuka wakaru darou, "You’ll understand someday")
- いつか会えると信じている (itsuka aeru to shinjite iru, "I believe we’ll meet someday")

explanation.en: Particle さえ marks something as 'even / surprisingly': 'even X (let alone the rest)'. こころの行方さえ知らず 'without even knowing where my heart's gone'. Often combined with negative or surprising statements.
explanation.es: La partícula さえ marca 'incluso / hasta': 'incluso X (por no hablar del resto)'. こころの行方さえ知らず 'sin saber siquiera dónde quedó mi corazón'.
explanation.pt-BR: Partícula さえ marca algo como 'até / até mesmo': 'até X (sem falar do resto)'. こころの行方さえ知らず 'sem nem saber para onde foi meu coração'.

explanation.en: Noun + ごと means 'together with X / including X (within the action)'. 恐怖ごと胸を焦がす 'burn the chest along with the fear'. The whole thing — fear and chest, game and everything in it — is treated as one unit.
explanation.es: Sustantivo + ごと significa 'junto con X / incluyendo X (en la acción)'. 恐怖ごと胸を焦がす 'quemar el pecho junto con el miedo'.
explanation.pt-BR: Substantivo + ごと significa 'junto com X / incluindo X (na ação)'. 恐怖ごと胸を焦がす 'queimar o peito junto com o medo'.

grammar_points.name: 〜なくていい (don't have to / it's fine if not)

explanation.en: Negative -te-form + いい means 'it's fine if not / don't have to'. 笑えなくていい 'it's fine if I can't laugh'; 許せなくていい 'fine if I can't forgive'. Permission to remain in the negative state.
explanation.es: Forma negativa -te + いい significa 'no pasa nada si no / no hace falta'. 笑えなくていい 'está bien si no puedo reír'; 許せなくていい 'está bien si no puedo perdonar'.
explanation.pt-BR: Forma negativa -te + いい significa 'tudo bem se não / não precisa'. 笑えなくていい 'tudo bem se não conseguir rir'; 許せなくていい 'tudo bem se não puder perdoar'.

explanation.en: Verb stem + たい means 'want to do X'. 連れていきたい 'want to take with me'; 護りぬきたい 'want to protect to the end'. The 〜たい form itself conjugates like an い-adjective.
explanation.es: Raíz del verbo + たい significa 'querer hacer X'. 連れていきたい 'quiero llevar conmigo'; 護りぬきたい 'quiero proteger hasta el final'. La forma 〜たい se conjuga como adjetivo い.
explanation.pt-BR: Radical do verbo + たい significa 'querer fazer X'. 連れていきたい 'quero levar comigo'; 護りぬきたい 'quero proteger até o fim'. A forma 〜たい conjuga como adjetivo い.

explanation.en: Verb stem + 抜く means 'do all the way through / to the bitter end'. 護りぬく 'protect to the very end'; やりぬく 'see something through'. Stresses persistence and completion.
explanation.es: Raíz del verbo + 抜く significa 'hacer hasta el final'. 護りぬく 'proteger hasta el final'; やりぬく 'llevar a término'.
explanation.pt-BR: Radical do verbo + 抜く significa 'fazer até o fim'. 護りぬく 'proteger até o fim'; やりぬく 'ir até o final'.

grammar_points.name: 〜たまま (in the state of, leaving X as is)

explanation.en: Past form + まま describes a sustained state: 'while remaining X / leaving X unchanged'. 失くしたまま 'while still losing'; 開けたまま 'with (the door) still open'. Often pairs with another verb that contrasts with the static state.
explanation.es: Forma pasada + まま describe estado sostenido: 'permaneciendo así / dejando como está'. 失くしたまま 'mientras lo pierdo'; 開けたまま 'con (la puerta) aún abierta'.
explanation.pt-BR: Forma passada + まま descreve estado mantido: 'continuando assim / deixando como está'. 失くしたまま 'enquanto ainda perde'; 開けたまま 'com (a porta) ainda aberta'.

translations.en: No matter what time it is —
translations.es: No importa el momento —
translations.pt-BR: Não importa o momento —

literal_meaning.en: 'What-kind-of time even.' どんな〜だって is a fixed pattern: 'no matter what (X)'. The line opens the song as an unconditional promise.

cultural_context.en: Hikari (光, 'Light') is the Japanese theme song of Kingdom Hearts (2002). The English version 'Simple and Clean' became a global gaming anthem; the original Japanese is softer, more intimate — about partnership, not just adventure.

translations.en: all by myself,
translations.es: completamente sola,
translations.pt-BR: completamente sozinha,

literal_meaning.en: 'Only one-person with.' たった一人 = 'just one and only' — emphatic 'all alone'.

translations.en: I'd been forgetting fate,
translations.es: olvidé el destino,
translations.pt-BR: esqueci o destino,

literal_meaning.en: 'Fate forgetting.' Te-form chains into the next verse. 運命忘れて (with the を particle dropped colloquially) = 'forgetting fate / putting destiny aside'.

meaning.en: have been living (生きる + 〜てくる perfective)

translations.en: and I'd been living that way — yet,
translations.es: y había vivido así — y sin embargo,
translations.pt-BR: e vinha vivendo desse jeito — e mesmo assim,

literal_meaning.en: 'Living-came although.' 〜てくる as a perfect: 'have come to (do X) up to now'. のに sets up the contrast — 'I'd been managing alone, BUT...'.

translations.en: in a sudden burst of light, I open my eyes —
translations.es: en medio de una luz repentina, abro los ojos —
translations.pt-BR: no meio de uma luz repentina, eu acordo —

literal_meaning.en: 'Sudden of light of inside, eyes [subj] wake.' 目が覚める ('eyes wake') is the standard idiom for waking up. 突然の光 = 'a sudden light' (with の linking adverb to noun).

translations.en: in the middle of the night.
translations.es: en plena medianoche.
translations.pt-BR: no meio da noite.

literal_meaning.en: 'Midnight at.' 真夜中 = 真 (deep) + 夜中 (middle of night) — the very deepest hour.

translations.en: Standing quietly at the exit,
translations.es: De pie, en silencio, junto a la salida,
translations.pt-BR: Em pé, em silêncio, na saída,

literal_meaning.en: 'Quietly exit at standing.' Te-form chains forward. 静かに sets the cinematic mood — the singer poised on a threshold.

translations.en: fire light into the darkness!
translations.es: ¡dispara luz a la oscuridad!
translations.pt-BR: dispare luz na escuridão!

literal_meaning.en: 'Darkness into light [obj] fire!' 撃つ specifically means 'to shoot (a gun, an arrow)'. The bare imperative 撃て gives the line a battle-cry edge — uncharacteristic for an Utada ballad.

translations.en: These days, things like 'promises' —
translations.es: Hoy en día, cosas como las "promesas" —
translations.pt-BR: Hoje em dia, coisas como "promessas" —

literal_meaning.en: 'These-days promise things-like.' なんて dismissively introduces 約束 — 'promises and so on'. Sets up the next verse's hesitation.

meaning.en: to make (someone do); cause (causative of する)

translations.en: do they just make us anxious, I wonder?
translations.es: ¿no será que solo nos ponen ansiosos?
translations.pt-BR: será que só servem pra deixar a gente ansiosa?

literal_meaning.en: 'Anxious make-do only I-wonder.' 不安にさせる = causative 'make (someone) anxious'. 〜だけ + かな = 'I wonder if it's just (X)'.

meaning.en: into (here in idiom 口にする)
want to do (たい-form of する)

translations.en: I just want to put the wish into words, that's all.
translations.es: Solo quiero ponerle palabras al deseo, nada más.
translations.pt-BR: Eu só quero pôr o desejo em palavras, é só isso.

literal_meaning.en: 'Wish [obj] mouth into want-to-do only [emph].' 口にする = 'to mention; to put into words'. だけ + さ = 'it's just only X' — defensive softening.

translations.en: I'll introduce you to my family, you know.
translations.es: Te voy a presentar a mi familia, ¿sabes?
translations.pt-BR: Vou te apresentar para a minha família, viu.

literal_meaning.en: 'Family to-also introduce [emph].' にも = 'to (the family) too / even'. 紹介する is the suru-verb 'to introduce'.

translations.en: It'll all work out, for sure.
translations.es: Saldrá todo bien, seguro.
translations.pt-BR: Vai dar tudo certo, com certeza.

literal_meaning.en: 'Surely well-go [emph].' うまくいく is one of Japanese's most useful idioms — '(things) go smoothly / work out'.

meaning.en: two people; the two of us

translations.en: the two of us, all along.
translations.es: los dos, siempre juntos.
translations.pt-BR: nós dois, sempre juntos.

literal_meaning.en: 'All-along two-people with.' Closes the first chorus — completes the v1 'no matter what time it is' with 'we'll be together'.

meaning.en: side; near (also read がわ for 'side of')

translations.en: I'll be by your side, so —
translations.es: Voy a estar a tu lado, así que —
translations.pt-BR: Vou estar do seu lado, então —

literal_meaning.en: 'Near at to-be because.' 側にいる = 'to be near (someone)'. The clause-final から carries the implied promise — 'so don't worry'.

meaning.en: called; named (X-という-Y = 'a Y called X')

translations.en: the light called 'you' will find me
translations.es: la luz llamada "tú" me va a encontrar
translations.pt-BR: a luz chamada "você" vai me encontrar

literal_meaning.en: 'You called light [subj] me [obj] find.' 君という光 — the noun phrase 'the light that is you'. 〜という is how Japanese names or defines: 'a Y called X'.

cultural_context.en: 君という光 is the song's emotional centre — and the title's grammatical reverse. The light isn't somewhere out there; it's the other person.

translations.en: Heading into the noisy street,
translations.es: Entrando a una calle ruidosa,
translations.pt-BR: Entrando numa rua barulhenta,

literal_meaning.en: 'Noisy street into entering.' Te-form chains into v18. The image: a quiet inner moment opening onto the loud public world.

meaning.en: take it off! (imperative of 取る)

translations.en: take off the mask of fate!
translations.es: ¡quítate la máscara del destino!
translations.pt-BR: tira a máscara do destino!

literal_meaning.en: 'Fate of mask [obj] take-off!' Bare imperative とれ. 仮面をとる is a direct translation of 'remove the mask' — drop the pretense.

meaning.en: doing too much (する + 過ぎ)

translations.en: Things like over-anticipating —
translations.es: Eso de andar adelantando todo —
translations.pt-BR: Esse negócio de ficar antecipando demais —

literal_meaning.en: 'Reading-ahead of doing-too-much things-like.' 先読み = literally 'reading what comes ahead' — predicting outcomes. The dismissive なんて scoffs at it.

translations.en: let's stop with the things that are pointless.
translations.es: dejemos de hacer cosas sin sentido.
translations.pt-BR: vamos parar com as coisas que não fazem sentido.

literal_meaning.en: 'Meaning of nothing thing [topic] stop.' 意味のない = 'meaningless / pointless'. Te-form 止めて without ください — soft request.

translations.en: Today, let's just eat something delicious.
translations.es: Hoy, vamos a comer algo rico.
translations.pt-BR: Hoje, vamos comer uma coisa gostosa.

literal_meaning.en: 'Today [topic] delicious things [obj] let's-eat [emph].' Volitional + よ adds gentle insistence. The line lands as the song's quiet philosophy: skip the existential dread, share a meal.

cultural_context.en: This verse is famous — it captures Utada's signature trick of placing a deeply ordinary line ('let's eat something good') against a cosmic backdrop. The mundane act becomes the act of love.

translations.en: The future's still way ahead.
translations.es: El futuro aún está muy adelante.
translations.pt-BR: O futuro ainda está bem mais à frente.

literal_meaning.en: 'Future [topic] way-ahead is [emph].' ずっと先 = 'far far ahead'. Implied: don't try to plan it all now.

meaning.en: I don't know (negative of 分かる)

translations.en: Even I don't know what comes.
translations.es: Ni yo sé lo que viene.
translations.pt-BR: Nem eu sei o que vem.

literal_meaning.en: 'I to-also don't-know.' 〜にも = 'even to (X)'. The speaker admits to not knowing — paired with 'so let's not worry about planning the future right now'.

translations.en: Don't try to finish it all,
translations.es: No intentes terminarlo todo,
translations.pt-BR: Não tente concluir tudo,

literal_meaning.en: 'Completion don't-make-do.' 完成させる is causative 'to make (X) be completed' — to wrap up. 〜ないで is 'please don't'.

meaning.en: (let's) make it better (te-form of 良くする)

translations.en: let's keep making it better.
translations.es: vamos haciéndolo mejor.
translations.pt-BR: vamos continuar deixando melhor.

literal_meaning.en: 'More make-good.' 良くする is i-adj 良い + する → 'to make (X) good'. Te-form 良くして acts as a soft request.

translations.en: Filming one scene at a time —
translations.es: Filmando una escena a la vez —
translations.pt-BR: Filmando uma cena de cada vez —

literal_meaning.en: 'One-scene each filming.' ずつ = 'X at a time / X each'. 撮る is the verb specifically for taking photos or filming.

translations.en: all we have to do is go on like that.
translations.es: basta con que sigamos así.
translations.pt-BR: basta a gente seguir assim.

literal_meaning.en: 'Go-if good because.' 〜ばいい = 'it's enough to / all (one) needs to do is'. Closes the sentence: '(filming one scene at a time), going like that is fine'.

meaning.en: to project; cast onto (映す + 出す)

translations.en: the light called 'you' projects my screenplay.
translations.es: la luz llamada "tú" proyecta mi guion.
translations.pt-BR: a luz chamada "você" projeta o meu roteiro.

literal_meaning.en: 'You called light [subj] my of script project-out.' 映し出す = 映す ('to project') + 出す ('to put out') — to cast onto a screen, vividly.

translations.en: Let's talk more —
translations.es: Hablemos más —
translations.pt-BR: Vamos conversar mais —

literal_meaning.en: 'More let's-talk [emph].' Volitional 話そう (from 話す) + よ — gentle persuasion.

translations.en: about tomorrow, right around the corner,
translations.es: sobre el mañana que está a la vuelta,
translations.pt-BR: sobre o amanhã, ali na esquina,

literal_meaning.en: 'Right-in-front of tomorrow of things-also.' 目前 (literally 'before the eyes') = 'imminent / about to happen'. ことも links to v29 — '(let's talk) about tomorrow's things, too'.

translations.en: switch off the TV,
translations.es: apaga la tele,
translations.pt-BR: desliga a TV,

literal_meaning.en: 'TV turn-off.' Te-form as soft imperative — '(please) turn off the TV'. The most domestic, intimate image of the song.

meaning.en: stay watching (request: te-form of 見ている + よ)

translations.en: and look at only me.
translations.es: y mírame solo a mí.
translations.pt-BR: e olha só pra mim.

literal_meaning.en: 'Me of things only [obj] keep-watching [emph].' 〜のこと is the standard way to refer to a person in casual speech ('matters concerning X'). 見ていて = 'keep watching' (te-form of continuous 見ている).

translations.en: No matter how good (anything) is,
translations.es: Por más buena que sea cualquier cosa,
translations.pt-BR: Por mais boa que seja qualquer coisa,

literal_meaning.en: 'How-much good-even-if.' 〜たって is the colloquial collapse of 〜ても. 良くたって = 良くても = 'even if it's good'. どんなに stacks 'no matter how'.

meaning.en: can't fully believe (信じる + 〜きれない)

translations.en: I can't quite bring myself to believe it.
translations.es: no termino de creérmelo.
translations.pt-BR: não consigo acreditar de verdade.

literal_meaning.en: 'Believe-cannot-completely [agree].' 〜きれない negates 〜きる ('do completely') → 'cannot do (X) all the way'. The line lands as half-confession, half-shared knowledge.

translations.en: Even at moments like those —
translations.es: Incluso en esos momentos —
translations.pt-BR: Mesmo em momentos assim —

literal_meaning.en: 'Such time even.' Variation on v1's どんな時だって — 'even (in moments) like THAT'. The chorus comes back with promise.

grammar_points.name: 〜だって (even; no matter)

explanation.en:
〜だって is the colloquial collapse of だ + って, used to mean 'even (X)' or 'no matter (X)'. After question words like どんな or いつ, it forms unconditional concessions: 'no matter what time / no matter what kind'.

This song opens with どんな時だって ('no matter what time it is') and echoes it later as そんな時だって ('even at moments like that'). Both function as openers to a promise: I'll be there.

Distinguish from だって as 'because' (sentence-initial, casual reason) and だって as 'X also (does)' (after a noun). Other typical examples: 誰だって知ってる ('everyone knows'), 雨の日だって出かける ('I go out even on rainy days'), 冬だって泳ぐ ('I swim even in winter'), どこだって行く ('I'll go anywhere').

grammar_points.conjugation_path: noun / question word + だって; for verbs/adjectives use 〜たって (verb-past + たって)

grammar_points.name: 〜なんて (dismissive 'things like')

explanation.en:
なんて attaches to a noun or verb to introduce something dismissively — 'things like (X)' or 'such a (X)'. It carries a tone of 'pfft, that's not worth much'. With negative predicates it intensifies the dismissal.

This song uses it in 約束なんて ('promises and the like') and 先読みのし過ぎなんて ('over-anticipating things and that'). Both phrases scoff at the named thing before the song moves toward what matters more.

Distinguish from なんて as 'how (X)!' (exclamation) and なんて as 'what?'. Other typical examples: お金なんていらない ('I don't need money or anything'), 嘘なんて言わない ('I'd never lie'), 結婚なんて考えていない ('I'm not even thinking about marriage'), 怖いなんて思わない ('I don't think it's scary at all').

grammar_points.conjugation_path: noun / verb (plain form) + なんて

grammar_points.name: Bare imperative — 撃て, とれ

explanation.en:
Japanese has a stark imperative form for direct commands. Group 1 verbs shift -u to -e (撃つ → 撃て, 取る → とれ). Group 2 verbs shift -る to -ろ. Irregulars: する → しろ, 来る → 来い.

This song fires off two bare imperatives in surprising places — 暗闇に光を撃て ('fire light into the darkness!') and 運命の仮面をとれ ('take off the mask of fate!'). The form is uncharacteristically rough for Utada's intimate style; it cuts through the song's quietness with sudden urgency.

Other typical examples: 待て ('wait!'), 見ろ ('look!'), 頑張れ ('do your best!'), 行け ('go!'), 来い ('come here!').

grammar_points.conjugation_path: Group 1: -u → -e (撃つ → 撃て); Group 2: -る → -ろ; する → しろ, 来る → 来い

grammar_points.name: 〜きれない (can't fully / can't completely)

explanation.en:
〜きれない is the negative of 〜きる. The suffix 切る (kiru) attached to a verb's i-stem means 'do (X) completely / through to the end'; negating it (〜きれない) means 'cannot do (X) fully'.

This song uses 信じきれない ('can't quite bring myself to believe'). The form is gentler than 信じられない ('can't believe at all') — the speaker isn't denying belief, just admitting they can't go all the way.

Other typical examples: 食べきれない ('I can't finish eating'), 数えきれない ('countless'), 言いきれない ('I can't say definitively'), 待ちきれない ('I can't wait any longer').

grammar_points.conjugation_path: verb (i-stem) + きれない (negative of 〜きる)

grammar_points.name: 〜という (X called Y; the X that is Y)

explanation.en:
X + という + Y is the standard pattern for 'a Y called X' or 'the Y that is X'. The という comes from と (quotative) + 言う ('to say') — literally 'a Y said-to-be-X'. Used to define, name, or appose.

This song features it twice in the chorus's emotional core: 君という光 ('the light called you / the light that is you'). The construction equates 'you' with 'light' through という — a bold poetic merger.

Other typical examples: 田中という人 ('a person named Tanaka'), 愛という言葉 ('the word called love'), 時間という宝 ('the treasure that is time'), 桜という花 ('the flower called sakura').

grammar_points.conjugation_path: noun X + という + noun Y

grammar_points.name: 〜ばいい (it's enough to / all you have to do is)

explanation.en:
〜ばいい combines the conditional 〜ば with いい ('good') to express 'it's enough / sufficient to (do X)' or 'all (one) needs to do is (X)'. Often used to suggest a course of action without forcing it.

This song uses it in ワンシーンずつ撮っていけばいいから ('all we have to do is keep filming one scene at a time'). The 〜ばいいから adds 'so don't worry' to the suggestion.

Other typical examples: わからなければ聞けばいい ('if you don't understand, just ask'), 嫌ならやめればいい ('if you don't like it, just quit'), 早く寝ればいい ('all you have to do is go to bed early'), 自分のやりたいようにやればいい ('just do it however you want').

grammar_points.conjugation_path: verb (conditional 〜ば) + いい

explanation.es: Grupo 1: -u → -areru (洗い流す → 洗い流される). Grupo 2: -る → -rareru. Pasado: 〜された / 〜られた. Las letras suelen usar la pasiva para cosas hechas al narrador.

translations.pt-BR: Pétalas caindo dançantes, flutuando —

literal_meaning.en: 'Flutter-fall petals flutter-flutter.' ヒラヒラ mimics light, thin objects (paper, cloth, petals) drifting in the air.

meaning.en: heart (心 written in katakana for tone)
slips through (contracted すり抜けていく)

translations.en: slipping through the cracks of my heart.
translations.es: colándose por las grietas de mi corazón.
translations.pt-BR: passando pelas frestas do meu coração.

literal_meaning.en: 'Heart of gap slip-through-go.' すり抜ける = すり (sliding) + 抜ける (pass through). The 〜てく contraction makes the slipping ongoing/forward.

meaning.en: have to become (colloquial of ならなければ)

translations.en: I have to be honest about it.
translations.es: Tengo que ser sincera.
translations.pt-BR: Eu preciso ser sincera.

literal_meaning.en: 'Honest become-must.' 素直になる = 'to become honest / open'. なんなきゃ is the colloquial collapse of ならなければ — a strong 'must'.

meaning.en: even if it strikes (te-form of 襲う + も)

translations.en: No matter what kind of pain hits my heart again,
translations.es: Pase lo que pase, no importa qué dolor vuelva a azotar mi corazón,
translations.pt-BR: Não importa que dor venha de novo atacar meu coração,

literal_meaning.en: 'What-kind-of pain [subj] again, my heart strike-even-if.' 〜ても is the concessive 'even if'. どんな〜が〜ても = 'whatever (X) does to me'.

meaning.en: shut tight (passive past of 閉ざす)

translations.en: I'll go see what's beyond
translations.es: Voy a ver lo que hay más allá
translations.pt-BR: Vou ver o que há além

literal_meaning.en: 'Shut-tight door of.' 閉ざす is a literary intransitive 'to shut firmly' — stronger than 閉める. The verse continues into v17.

translations.en: of that tightly-shut door — I'm going.
translations.es: de esa puerta cerrada — voy a ir.
translations.pt-BR: daquela porta fechada — eu vou.

literal_meaning.en: 'Other-side [obj] go-to-see [emph].' 〜にいく chain = 'go (in order) to (do X)'. The clause-final から here doesn't mark 'because' but adds firm assertive — 'so I will, mark my words'.

translations.en: Two people who were complete opposites,
translations.es: Dos personas que eran totalmente opuestas,
translations.pt-BR: Duas pessoas que eram totalmente opostas,

literal_meaning.en: 'Completely opposite of two-people.' まるで is an intensifier — here it strengthens 正反対 ('exact opposite'). The line stands alone as a noun phrase.

translations.en: but somehow — when we're together, before I knew it —
translations.es: pero quién sabe por qué — cuando estamos juntos, sin que me dé cuenta —
translations.pt-BR: mas, sei lá por quê — quando estamos juntos, sem eu perceber —

literal_meaning.en: 'But why-it-is, together be when, before-I-knew.' 〜と as a conditional means 'when / whenever (X)'. いつの間にか = 'in some span of time I didn't notice'.

translations.en: the bits where we're alike kept growing, didn't they?
translations.es: fueron creciendo las cosas en que nos parecemos, ¿verdad?
translations.pt-BR: foram aumentando as coisas em que somos parecidos, né?

literal_meaning.en: 'Resemble bits also increased [agree].' 似ているところ → 似てるとこ — colloquial drops both い and the formal ろ. ね seeks agreement.

meaning.en: had been imitating each other (真似 + 〜合う + ていた)

translations.en: ...or so (we said) — but really, we were copying each other a little.
translations.es: ...pero, en realidad, nos estábamos imitando un poco.
translations.pt-BR: ...mas, na real, a gente estava se imitando um pouco.

literal_meaning.en: 'Such-things really [topic] a-little imitate-mutually-was.' 真似する = 'to imitate'; 〜合う = 'to do together / mutually'; 〜ていた = past continuous.

translations.en: On the night you were crying,
translations.es: La noche en que llorabas,
translations.pt-BR: Na noite em que você chorava,

literal_meaning.en: 'You [subj] was-crying night.' 泣いてた = 泣いていた contracted. The whole clause modifies 夜 as a relative clause.

translations.en: I wiped your tears.
translations.es: Te sequé las lágrimas.
translations.pt-BR: Eu enxuguei suas lágrimas.

literal_meaning.en: 'I [topic] tears [obj] wiped.' Plain past sentence — direct, intimate.

meaning.en: nodding to each other (te-form of うなずき合う)

translations.en: Nodding lightly to each other —
translations.es: Asintiendo levemente uno al otro —
translations.pt-BR: Concordando levemente um com o outro —

literal_meaning.en: 'Easily nod-mutually-and.' 〜合う suffix once again — both people doing the same gesture together.

translations.en: I noticed the future I'd been running from —
translations.es: Me di cuenta del futuro del que estaba huyendo —
translations.pt-BR: Percebi o futuro do qual eu estava fugindo —

literal_meaning.en: 'Run-away future to notice.' 逃げる未来 = 'a future (one is) running from' — relative clause. 〜に気が付く = 'to notice / become aware of (X)'.

translations.en: Gazing at the unchanging you,
translations.es: Mirando fijamente al tú que no cambia,
translations.pt-BR: Encarando você, que segue igual,

literal_meaning.en: 'Doesn't-change you [obj] gaze-and.' 変わらないキミ = 'the you who doesn't change' — present-tense relative clause.

meaning.en: let's leave (it) behind (置く + ていく volitional)

translations.en: I decided to leave the memories behind.
translations.es: Decidí dejar atrás los recuerdos.
translations.pt-BR: Decidi deixar as lembranças para trás.

literal_meaning.en: 'Memories [topic] leave-go [quotative] decided.' Volitional + と + 決める = 'decide that (one) will (do X)'. The volitional acts as the inner thought.

translations.en: Sorry — I'm going on ahead now.
translations.es: Perdón — me adelanto.
translations.pt-BR: Desculpa — vou na frente agora.

literal_meaning.en: 'Sorry, now ahead to go [emph].' 先に行く is the formula said when leaving before someone — at work, on a date, on a journey. Loaded with farewell weight here.

translations.en: Petals fluttering down, swaying-swaying —
translations.es: Pétalos cayendo, meciéndose —
translations.pt-BR: Pétalas caindo dançantes, balançando —

literal_meaning.en: 'Flutter-fall petals sway-sway.' Variant of v12 — same sentence, ヒラヒラ replaced by ユラユラ. The shift suggests a slower, more deliberate motion.

meaning.en: stay holding (te-form of 繋いでいる, contracted; soft request)

translations.en: Keep holding my swaying heart —
translations.es: Sigue sosteniendo este corazón que tiembla —
translations.pt-BR: Continue segurando esse coração que treme —

literal_meaning.en: 'Sway heart, holding-be (please).' 繋いでて is 繋いでいて contracted — 'stay holding'. Used as a soft imperative 'please keep doing X'.

translations.en: so that I don't forget,
translations.es: para no olvidar,
translations.pt-BR: para não esquecer,

literal_meaning.en: 'Forget-not so-that.' 〜ないように = 'so that (X) doesn't happen' — purpose clause attached to a negative.

meaning.en: to start walking (歩く + 出す inceptive)

translations.en: I set my dreams and wishes on the spring wind, and I start walking.
translations.es: Pongo mis sueños y deseos en el viento de primavera, y empiezo a caminar.
translations.pt-BR: Coloco meus sonhos e desejos no vento da primavera, e começo a andar.

literal_meaning.en: 'Spring-wind on dream and wish [obj] load, start-walking.' 〜出す attached to a verb stem = 'start (doing X)' suddenly. The closing image: setting hopes adrift on the wind to journey on.

translations.en: Hey — lift up your face,
translations.es: Oye — levanta la cara,
translations.pt-BR: Ei — levanta o rosto,

literal_meaning.en: 'Hey, face [obj] lift.' 顔をあげる is the literal 'raise one's face' — lift one's eyes from the ground. Common idiom for 'cheer up / look ahead'.

translations.en: so that we can laugh side by side again.
translations.es: para que podamos volver a reír uno al lado del otro.
translations.pt-BR: para que possamos rir lado a lado de novo.

literal_meaning.en: 'Again next-to at can-laugh so-that.' 笑える is the potential of 笑う ('to laugh'); 〜ように with potential = purpose 'so that one can'.

translations.en: No one is really strong, you know.
translations.es: Nadie es realmente fuerte, ¿sabes?
translations.pt-BR: Ninguém é forte de verdade, sabe.

literal_meaning.en: 'Anyone strong things-like is-not (it's that).' なんて attached to an i-adj stem dismissively + ない = 'isn't anything like (X)'. Confessional tone.

translations.en: Being alone is scary — me too.
translations.es: Estar solo da miedo — a mí también.
translations.pt-BR: Estar sozinho dá medo — comigo também.

literal_meaning.en: 'Alone if uneasy is [emph], I-even so.' 〜だって = 'even (X) is the same way' — admitting shared vulnerability. The whole verse is the emotional core.

translations.en: (So that) the future I believed in
translations.es: (Para que) el futuro en el que creí
translations.pt-BR: (Para que) o futuro em que acreditei

literal_meaning.en: 'Believed future [subj].' 信じた未来 — relative clause: 'the future (one) believed in'. Sentence trails into v38.

translations.en: may begin here, again.
translations.es: vuelva a comenzar, desde aquí.
translations.pt-BR: comece outra vez, daqui.

literal_meaning.en: 'Here-from again begin so-that.' Final 〜ように at the end of a sentence functions as a wish — 'may (X)'. Closes the song on a quiet prayer.

cultural_context.en: Sentence-final 〜ように without a main clause is a Japanese way of phrasing a wish or prayer (神様、〜ますように 'God, may it be that...'). Closes the song with the resigned hope of a Shinto prayer.

grammar_points.name: 〜なきゃ (colloquial 'have to / must')

explanation.en:
〜なきゃ is the colloquial collapse of 〜なければ(ならない/いけない) — 'must / have to'. It attaches to a verb's negative stem (drop い from 〜ない) plus 〜きゃ. The 'ならない' tail is dropped in casual speech, leaving the obligation implied.

This song uses it twice in close succession: 伝えなきゃ ('I have to tell you') and 素直になんなきゃ ('I have to be honest'). Both are inner thoughts — the speaker is talking to herself.

Note that ならない collapses to なんない (a dialectal/casual form), giving 素直になんなきゃ instead of 素直にならなきゃ. Other typical examples: 行かなきゃ ('I have to go'), 早く起きなきゃ ('I have to get up early'), 食べなきゃダメだよ ('you have to eat').

grammar_points.conjugation_path: verb (negative stem 〜ない, drop い) + きゃ; full form: 〜なければ(ならない)

grammar_points.name: 〜ながら (while doing)

explanation.en:
〜ながら attaches to a verb's i-stem (連用形) to express two simultaneous actions or states by the same subject: 'doing X while doing Y'. The main action is in the second clause; ながら marks the secondary, ongoing action.

This song uses it in 伝えなきゃと思いながら ('while thinking I have to tell you'), pairing the inner monologue with the outer action of letting time slip by.

Other typical examples: 音楽を聴きながら勉強する ('to study while listening to music'), 笑いながら泣く ('to laugh and cry at once'), 歩きながら話す ('to talk while walking'), 涙を流しながら謝った ('she apologised in tears').

grammar_points.conjugation_path: verb (i-stem / 連用形) + ながら

grammar_points.name: Volitional + と思う / と決める (decide that I will...)

explanation.en:
Verb in volitional form (〜よう/〜う) + と + 思う ('think') or 決める ('decide') expresses an inner resolve: 'I think I'll (do X)' or 'I decided to (do X)'. The volitional acts as quoted direct thought.

This song uses it in 思い出は置いていこうと決めた ('I decided I'll leave the memories behind'). The volitional 置いていこう encodes the speaker's willed plan; と marks it as quoted thought; 決めた seals the decision.

Other typical examples: 日本に行こうと思う ('I'm thinking of going to Japan'), 早く寝ようと決めた ('I decided to go to bed early'), 諦めようと思った ('I thought about giving up'), 結婚しようと決めた ('we decided we'd get married').

grammar_points.conjugation_path: verb (volitional 〜よう/〜う) + と + 思う / 決める / する (try to)

grammar_points.name: 〜ても / 〜でも (even if; even when)

explanation.en:
Adding も to a verb's te-form creates the concessive 'even if (X)'. Often pairs with question words (どんな, 何, 誰) to express 'no matter what / whoever / however'.

This song uses どんな痛みがまた 僕のココロ襲っても ('no matter what kind of pain hits my heart again'). The どんな〜が〜ても construction creates an unconditional concession — the speaker promises to act regardless of what comes.

Other typical examples: 雨が降っても行く ('I'll go even if it rains'), 高くても買う ('I'll buy it even if it's expensive'), 誰が反対しても決めた ('I've decided no matter who objects').

grammar_points.conjugation_path: verb (te-form) + も; i-adj (-くて) + も = -くても; na-adj/noun + でも

grammar_points.name: 〜ように (so that / may it be that)

explanation.en:
〜ように has two main uses: (1) attached mid-sentence, it marks purpose — 'so that (X) happens'; (2) at the end of a sentence, it expresses a wish or prayer — 'may it be that (X)'.

This song uses both forms. Mid-sentence purposes: 忘れないように ('so that I don't forget'), 笑えるように ('so that we can laugh'), 始まるように ('so that it begins'). The closing line of the song — ここからまた 始まるように — uses the wish form: 'may it begin here, again' as a quiet final prayer.

Other typical examples: 遅れないように出発する ('to leave so as not to be late'), 風邪をひかないように ('so as not to catch a cold'), 元気でありますように ('may you be well'), 雨が降りませんように ('please don't let it rain').

grammar_points.conjugation_path: verb (plain form, often potential or negative) + ように

grammar_points.name: 〜って (casual quotative)

explanation.en:
って is the colloquial spoken form of the quotative particle と. It can mark direct quotes, reported speech, or even topics (like a casual は). In song lyrics it's especially common because it lets singers slip in spoken words mid-line without breaking flow.

This song uses it twice in the verse-2 stanza: 「離れたくないなあ」って ('thinking 'I don't want to part''), 「明日ね」って さよならして ('saying 'see you tomorrow' as goodbye'). Both are inner-thought / spoken-word quotes; って lets the singer attribute them.

って can also mean 'they say that' (rumor) or replace は in casual definitions: 田中さんって優しい人だ ('Tanaka is a kind person'). Other typical examples: 行くって言ったよ ('she said she'd go'), 何って言うの? ('what are you saying?'), 月曜日って忙しい ('Mondays are busy, you know').

grammar_points.conjugation_path: any quoted phrase + って (replaces formal と)

grammar_points.name: 〜ざるを得ない (zaru wo enai: can't help but; have no choice but to)

explanation.en:
A formal/literary pattern meaning 'must, reluctantly / have no choice but to'. Attach to a verb's negative stem + ざる + を得ない. Irregular: する → せざる; 来る → 来ざる.

From this song: 認めざるを得ない = 'I have no choice but to admit it'.

More examples:
• 行かざるを得ない (no choice but to go)
• 同意せざるを得ない (must agree, reluctantly)
• 諦めざるを得ない (must give up)

grammar_points.conjugation_path: 認める → 認め (neg. stem) + ざる + を + 得ない → 認めざるを得ない

grammar_points.name: 〜させないでほしい (sasenaide hoshii: I want you not to make me)

explanation.en:
Causative + negative te-form + ほしい = 'I want you not to cause X / I'd rather you didn't make me do X'.

From this song: あんまり期待させないでほしい = 'I don't want you to make me hope too much'.

More examples:
• 心配させないでほしい (I don't want to make you worry / Don't worry me)
• 泣かせないで (Don't make (me/her) cry)
• 困らせないで (Don't trouble me)

grammar_points.name: Volitional 〜(よ)う (ou / you: let's / I will)

explanation.en:
Attach to a verb to suggest 'let's (do X)'. Godan: drop 〜u, add 〜ou (しよう, 踊ろう). Ichidan: drop 〜る, add 〜よう (生きよう).

From this song:
• 指輪をしよう (let's wear rings)
• 祝おう (let's celebrate)
• 踊ろう (let's dance)
• 誓おう (let's vow)

More examples:
• 食べよう (let's eat)
• 頑張ろう (let's try our best)
• 行こう (let's go)

grammar_points.conjugation_path: 祝う → 祝お + う → 祝おう

grammar_points.name: 〜たまま (ta mama: while still / in the state of)

explanation.en:
Attach 〜た (past) + まま to express 'while still X / in the state of having done X'.

From this song: しがみついたまま眠りたい = 'I want to sleep still clinging'.

More examples:
• 電気をつけたまま寝た (slept with the light still on)
• 立ったまま話す (speak while still standing)
• 靴を履いたまま (with shoes still on)

grammar_points.name: 〜くらい / 〜ぐらい (kurai / gurai: to the extent of)

explanation.en:
Attach to a verb/adjective/noun to express 'to the extent of / about / so much that'.

From this song: ダサいくらいしがみついた = 'clung so tight it was uncool'.

More examples:
• 泣くくらい嬉しい (so happy I could cry)
• 痛いくらい抱きしめる (hug so hard it hurts)
• 死ぬくらい疲れた (exhausted to the point of dying)

grammar_points.name: 〜でもない (de mo nai: not even / isn't)

explanation.en:
Attach 〜でもない after a noun to mean 'not even (X) / isn't (X)'. Often paired with 〜ではなく to contrast.

From this song: 約束でもない 誓いだよ = 'it's not even a promise — it's an oath'.

More examples:
• 嘘でもない (it's not a lie either)
• 大した話でもない (not much of a story)
• 誰でもない私 (me who is no one else)

grammar_points.name: 〜という (to iu: called / named / the one where)

explanation.en:
Attach to a noun to mean 'the X called / the X named / the fact of X'. Marks the identity or content of what precedes.

From this song: 今日という日 = 'this day called today / a day that is today'.

More examples:
• 田中という人 (a person called Tanaka)
• 愛という言葉 (the word "love")
• 合格したという知らせ (news that I passed)

grammar_points.name: Imperative form (blunt command: 〜え / 〜ろ)

explanation.en:
The blunt imperative — godan verbs drop 〜u and add 〜e (走る → 走れ, 走り出す → 走り出せ); ichidan verbs drop 〜る and add 〜ろ (食べる → 食べろ). Used for punch in songs; in real life it's quite rough.

From this song: 走り出せ = 'Start running!'; 伸ばせ = 'Reach out!'.

More examples:
• 見ろ (look!)
• 待て (wait!)
• 信じろ (believe!)

grammar_points.conjugation_path: 走り出す → 走り出せ; 伸ばす → 伸ばせ

explanation.en:
Literary/archaic negative. Attaches to a verb's negative stem, equivalent to 〜ないで. Common in songs and formal writing.

From this song:
• うまくいかず = 'without going well'
• 何も出来ず = 'unable to do anything'

More examples:
• 知らず = 'without knowing'
• 思わず = 'involuntarily'
• 休まず = 'without resting'

grammar_points.name: Potential verbs (〜eる / 〜られる: can do)

explanation.en:
Godan verbs: change 〜u to 〜eru (行く → 行ける). Ichidan verbs: 〜る → 〜られる (食べる → 食べられる). Means 'can / able to (do)'.

From this song:
• 見つけられない (can't find)
• 越えてゆける (can get across)
• 立ち止まれない (can't stop)
• つかめる (can grasp)

More examples:
• 話せる (can speak)
• 泳げる (can swim)
• 食べられる (can eat)

grammar_points.conjugation_path: 行く → 行ける; 食べる → 食べられる

grammar_points.name: 〜ば / 〜なければ (ba / nakereba: if / if not)

explanation.en:
Conditional form — godan: change 〜u → 〜eba. Ichidan: 〜る → 〜れば. Negative: 〜ない → 〜なければ = 'if (you) don't'.

From this song:
• 心一つにすれば = 'if (we) make our hearts one'
• 逃げ出さなければ = 'if we don't run away'

More examples:
• 時間があれば (if I have time)
• 頑張れば (if you try hard)
• 行かなければ (if you don't go)

grammar_points.conjugation_path: する → すれば; 逃げ出す → 逃げ出さなければ

grammar_points.name: 〜のまま (no mama: as-is / in the state of)

explanation.en:
Attach to a noun (via の) or a plain form to express 'staying as X / in the state of X / without change'.

From this song: 想いのまま = 'as my feelings are / letting my heart lead'.

More examples:
• そのまま (as it is)
• 昔のまま (the same as before)
• 気持ちのままに動く (move as one's heart dictates)

grammar_points.name: 〜ことなく (koto naku: without ever / without X-ing)

explanation.en:
Attach 〜ことなく after a verb's dictionary form to mean 'without (ever) X-ing'. Slightly literary; emphasizes a continuous state.

From this song: 止まることなく流れ続けてる = 'keeps flowing without ever stopping'.

More examples:
• 疑うことなく信じる (believe without doubting)
• 諦めることなく続ける (continue without giving up)
• 振り返ることなく歩む (walk on without looking back)

grammar_points.name: 〜てくれる (te kureru: does X for me)

explanation.en:
Attach to a verb's te-form to express 'someone does X for my benefit'. Marks directionality of the favor (inward, to the speaker).

From this song: 彩ってくれる = '(something/someone) colors (my path) for me'.

More examples:
• 教えてくれる (teach me)
• 助けてくれる (help me)
• 聞いてくれてありがとう (thank you for listening (for my sake))
